text:
nora.kim: quick sync from today's design huddle on dedicated-pool autoscale + policy compiler spike. want to capture decisions and next actions.

diego.santos: thanks. high level take: aim for a tiny, audit-able compile target that maps tenant policies into numeric goals + ranked actions. avoid encoding scheduling logic in the DSL.

priya: agree. also we should support a "burst budget" primitive so tenants can spend a fixed credit on short bursts without changing their long-term cost cap. example field: 
```
burst_budget_tokens: 3600  # seconds of burst at baseline replica
```

ollie: interesting. how does that interact with admission tokens and warmup credits? potential for double-spend.

nora.kim: plan: burst budget is consumed at operator when admission succeeds; warmup credits remain a separate accounting unit. compiler emits both as separate intent fields so operator reconciler can debit the right ledger.

diego.santos: operator compatibility concern: we mustn't require operator upgrades to accept old tokens. suggestion: compiled intents include a version + a short hash. operator ignores unknown fields and treats unrecognized versions as "best-effort" if feature-flagged.

priya: observability: every decision must include three refs: policy_id, compile_version, and decision_code. add those to existing tracing span so we can trace an eviction back to a policy line.

ollie: conflict resolution in multi-tenant pools? earlier proposals used priority buckets. i'd prefer deterministic arbitration: higher SLA tier wins; tie-break by weighted tenant score. keep it stable across restarts.

diego.santos: +1. also need soft vs hard distinctions. soft = target hint; hard = admission blocker. compiler should mark fields accordingly.

nora.kim: rollout:
1) schema + storage behind feature flag (store but no compile) for 10 days
2) add compiler that outputs primitive intent (p99_target_ms, cost_cap_usd, burst_budget, soft/hard flags) and enable in staging pools only for 1 week
3) operator extra-logging + policy provenance trace integrated into oncall alerts for 2 weeks
4) flip enforcement default after no regressions for 3 weeks

priya: metrics to watch: false-positive evictions, unexpected throttles, burst-budget burn rate, and policy-compile mismatch errors. we need dashboards before enforcement.

ollie: simulator needs one more capability: simulate mixed tenant policies in the same pool and compute fairness score + cost distribution. can reuse the cluster-sim harness but add policy resolver layer.

diego.santos: edgecases called out: thermal throttling + MIG fragmentation can make numerical goals unattainable; compiler should emit "feasibility_estimate" so operator can decide to degrade gracefully.

nora.kim: good point. feasibility_estimate is computed from recent pool telemetry; if estimate < threshold, operator triggers controlled fallback (quantize -> batch -> fallback-model) in the declared order. include that order in compiled intent.

priya: who owns the compiler PoC? diego for 4d spike to output intent proto + unit tests. ollie can add sim scenarios. nora will wire schema + storage. i'll own observability contract & dashboards.

runtime-bot: lint-check: new schema draft passes basic validation. feature-flag disabled.

nora.kim: thanks all. i'll post a short RFC addendum with the rollout timeline, sample schema, and monitoring checklist. tagging follow-ups: diego -> compiler spike, ollie -> sim scenarios, priya -> dashboard PR.

diego.santos: posting PR later today with proto sketch.

ollie: will spin up sim branch and share results next week.

priya: adding dashboard templates to the ops repo now.

nora.kim: perfect. we'll reconvene after the spike. :rocket:
